title: Management-clock synchronization with invariant shared-state hydrology

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-16 model or tests before DUMMY-15B closes and the implementation baseline is rebound.

purpose: Isolate management-clock/event-synchronization effects from physical timestep effects by holding the two-window physical trajectory and total realized managed withdrawal identical while changing only whether a mid-horizon priority event is observed.

canonical_setup.fast_management_clock: samples/updates priority at t=0 and t=0.5
canonical_setup.stale_management_clock: samples priority at t=0 and holds ROOT_FIRST through t=1

exact_window_1.note: To keep the first physical window from exhausting the root request, DUMMY-16 does not submit the full root deficit as one 0.5-window claim. It caps the scheduled root claim at 20 m3 for this clock experiment while retaining root-state bookkeeping.

invariants: Both schedules use identical physical window boundaries and the same requested total 40 m3 in each physical window.
Both schedules therefore have identical total realized managed withdrawal, V, surface head and groundwater head in each physical window.
The only difference is which managed recipient receives the scarce second-window water after the priority event.

Combined root+surface+groundwater storage loss equals cumulative supplied external demand, so the two schedules can have different represented-system storage despite identical surface/groundwater physical trajectories.
Root future demand differs because accepted root delivery differs, not because prior shortage is stored separately.
This first clock experiment does not compare physical timestep sizes and therefore does not reuse DUMMY-08 temporal-partition error as an explanation.
hypotheses: Fast event-synchronized priority sampling yields final root storage 60.4444444444 m3 and next root request 19.5555555556 m3.
Stale priority sampling yields final root storage 80 m3 and next root request 0.
Both schedules end with identical h_s=0.2 m and h_g=0.1955555556 m.
The difference in combined represented-system storage equals the difference in cumulative external supplied demand.
Exact conservation alone cannot distinguish the two management-clock semantics because each schedule closes its own correct ledger.
A priority event can therefore materially alter future hydrological demand without altering the shared surface/groundwater trajectory when total managed withdrawal is invariant.
interpretation_boundary: The 20 m3 scheduled root claim in window 1 is a controlled clock-experiment cap, not a production SWAP scheduling rule.
This work unit does not decide which management clock production Ribasim/SWAP coupling should use.
No physical timestep comparison is made in the first stage.
No network routing or real Ribasim allocation optimizer is represented.
future_extensions: move the priority event off the physical-window boundary and test event subdivision
separate root-demand refresh clock from allocation-priority clock
compare Ribasim allocation timestep, physical solver timestep, SWAP state timestep and outer commit window
introduce one exogenous demand event and one hydrological threshold event in the same outer window
authority_rebind_note: DUMMY-16 preregistration/concept were prepared while DUMMY-15B was blocked. No DUMMY-16 implementation existed. Baseline rebound to this post-DUMMY-15B closeout head before any DUMMY-16 code/tests.
